S5.01.needs: a signed-in account; the title row needs at least one message
S5.01.note: The title row is hidden when signed out and for temporary chats.
steps: Open the AGI side panel and sign in to a Managed Cloud account.
Send one message in the chat box.
Look at the top: the header shows the model button, Recent chats, New chat and More.
Look just below the header for the chat title row. Compare with Expected: the header shows where you are and the main actions.
S5.01.where: Side panel header: New chat, Recent chats and More buttons at the top; after the first message, the chat title shows in a row below the header

S5.02.note: The Chat / Computer Use tab bar is hidden in the chat view. No Projects, Code or Work mode was found in the code.
steps: Click inside the side panel.
Press Cmd+K on Mac (Ctrl+K on Windows).
Type Computer Use and pick it under Go to.
Look for the two tabs Chat and Computer Use at the top, with Computer Use active.
S5.02.where: Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on Mac) > type Computer Use > pick Computer Use under Go to

S5.07.needs: a signed-in account or saved chats on this device
S5.07.note: The search covers chats only. The Cmd+K palette also searches chats.
steps: Click the clock icon in the header (Recent chats).
Click the box labelled Search recent chats.
Type part of a chat title.
Look that only matching chats stay in the list.
S5.07.where: Recent chats (clock icon in the header) > Search recent chats box

S5.08.note: New chat is also in the Cmd+K palette.
steps: Open a chat that already has messages.
Click the New chat button in the header.
Look for an empty chat with no messages and no title row.
S5.08.where: Header > New chat button (icon at the top right of the side panel)

S5.10.note: The list holds chats only. No recent projects or tasks section was found here.
steps: Click the clock icon (Recent chats).
Look for the list of recent chats with dates.
Click one chat row.
Look that the chat opens in the chat view. Compare with Expected: recent items open on selection.
S5.10.where: Recent chats (clock icon in the header) > list of chat rows

steps: Click the clock icon (Recent chats).
Look at a row: the title and the date.
Look for the open chat: its row has a stronger background and is marked as the current page.
Click another row's title and look that its chat opens.
S5.13.where: Recent chats (clock icon in the header) > a chat row

S5.14.needs: a signed-in account with a project
S5.14.note: No project rows were found in the side panel navigation. Projects appear only in the @ mention menu under Projects and as a Project name chip. I searched apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts for project rows and Projects navigation.

S5.15.needs: a signed-in account that has background tasks
S5.15.note: Open takes you to the chat in the web app, not inside the side panel.
steps: Sign in to an AGI account.
Click the More button (⋮) at the top right.
Click Tasks.
Look for task rows with a title, a state and a time, and an Open button. Compare with Expected: tasks are shown apart from chats.

S5.17.needs: a signed-in account with a running task
S5.17.note: Recent chat rows have no running mark; the only one found is the state text in Tasks.
steps: Start a background task that is still running.
Click More (⋮) > Tasks.
Look for the state text Running under that task.
S5.17.where: More (⋮) > Tasks > the state text under a task

S5.18.needs: a signed-in account and a task that needs input or approval
S5.18.note: Recent chat rows have no waiting mark; the only one found is the state text in Tasks.
steps: Start a task that asks for your input or approval.
Click More (⋮) > Tasks.
Look for Waiting for input or Waiting for approval under that task.
S5.18.where: More (⋮) > Tasks > the state text under a task

S5.20.note: Which items appear depends on whether the chat is saved to the account. Archive and Delete ask to confirm first.
steps: Click the clock icon (Recent chats).
Click the ⋯ button at the right of a chat row.
Look for Pin, Rename, Move to project, Share, Archive and Delete chat.
Click Rename and look for the edit box.
S5.20.where: Recent chats (clock icon) > More actions (⋯) on a chat row

S5.26.needs: none; the Chats list needs a signed-in account
steps: Click inside the side panel.
Press Cmd+K (Ctrl+K on Windows).
Look for the Commands box with the placeholder Search commands and chats.
Type New or a chat name and look for matching Go to items and Chats.
S5.26.where: Cmd+K on Mac (Ctrl+K on Windows) with the side panel focused

S5.27.note: The list shows only Chrome commands. The Cmd+K palette shortcut is not listed. The More > Shortcuts item opens saved prompts, not this list.
steps: Click the More button (⋮).
Click Extension settings. The Options page opens in a new tab.
Click Options in the left list.
Scroll to Keyboard shortcuts. Look for Open side panel and Send page screenshot to Desktop, each with a shortcut and a Configure button.
S5.27.where: More (⋮) > Extension settings > Options page: Options > Keyboard shortcuts

S5.29.needs: a signed-in account; Usage is not shown on the Free plan
S5.29.note: The account block is hidden when signed out.
steps: Sign in to an AGI account.
Click the More button (⋮) at the top right.
Look at the top of the menu: your name or email and plan name.
Look for Settings, Usage, Tasks, Memory, Upgrade plan and Log out.
S5.29.where: More (⋮) > account block at the top of the menu

S5.30.note: No feedback entry was found in the Help menu or Help section.
steps: Click the More button (⋮).
Click Help. The Options page opens on its Help section.
Look for Help center, Documentation and Contact support.

S5.31.needs: a signed-in account on a plan that has a higher tier
S5.31.note: Upgrade plan shows only when a higher tier exists. The plan file says the quota upgrade button leads to web billing behind a waitlist gate; I did not check that path.
steps: Sign in to an account on a plan with a higher tier.
Click the More button (⋮).
Look for Upgrade plan and click it.
Look that a web plans page opens in a new tab.

labels.text: Desktop tools are optional and currently disconnected.

S5.32.needs: the AGI desktop app not running
S5.32.note: The notice covers desktop tools only. No general cloud connection indicator was found.
steps: Make sure the AGI desktop app is not running.
Open the side panel.
Look above the chat box for the notice text and the Reconnect button.
Click Reconnect and look for a change in the notice.
S5.32.where: Above the chat box: notice Desktop tools are optional and currently disconnected. > Reconnect

S5.35.needs: a narrow side panel; Chrome side panels cannot reach phone width
S5.35.note: No slide-in drawer was found in the code. Recent chats is a full overlay opened from a header button, with focus returned on close.
steps: Drag the Chrome side panel to its narrowest width.
Click the clock icon (Recent chats).
Look for the list filling the panel with a Close button.
Click Close and look that focus returns to the clock icon.
S5.35.where: Header > Recent chats (clock icon); the list opens as a full overlay over the panel
